import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Source file paths
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/test_1.csv"
    target_output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_49/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Columns expected in target and sources (all identical)
    columns = [
        'tripduration', 'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station id', 'start station name',
        'start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station id', 'end station name',
        'end station latitude', 'end station longitude', 'bikeid', 'usertype', 'birth year', 'gender'
    ]

    # Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

    # Ensure columns are exactly as expected and in the same order
    df0 = df0[columns]
    df1 = df1[columns]

    # Both source tables have the exact same schema as the target.
    # According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, we should UNION (concatenate) them.

    # Concatenate source tables vertically (union)
    df_union = pd.concat([df0, df1], ignore_index=True)

    # Data type enforcement according to target schema:
    # 'tripduration': integer
    # 'starttime': string
    # 'stoptime': string
    # 'start station id': integer
    # 'start station name': string
    # 'start station latitude': float
    # 'start station longitude': float
    # 'end station id': integer
    # 'end station name': string
    # 'end station latitude': float
    # 'end station longitude': float
    # 'bikeid': integer
    # 'usertype': string
    # 'birth year': integer
    # 'gender': integer

    # Convert columns to appropriate types, handling missing values carefully
    # For integer columns, convert with pd.to_numeric and downcast, coercing errors to NaN then fill or convert to Int64 dtype (nullable integer)
    int_columns = [
        'tripduration', 'start station id', 'end station id', 'bikeid', 'birth year', 'gender'
    ]
    float_columns = [
        'start station latitude', 'start station longitude', 'end station latitude', 'end station longitude'
    ]
    str_columns = [
        'starttime', 'stoptime', 'start station name', 'end station name', 'usertype'
    ]

    for col in int_columns:
        df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

    for col in float_columns:
        df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

    for col in str_columns:
        # Convert to string, fill NaN with empty string to avoid issues
        df_union[col] = df_union[col].astype(str).fillna('')

    # The target examples show starttime and stoptime with microseconds precision as strings.
    # The source data already has this format as string, so no conversion needed.

    # Final check: reorder columns to target schema order (already done, but just to be sure)
    df_union = df_union[columns]

    # Write the result to the target CSV file with header and no index
    df_union.to_csv(target_output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
